readiness_analysis.analysis_scope: Three readiness options presented for human decision per CLAUDE.md §7
readiness_analysis.decision_authority: None of these verdicts are binding; this agent documents candidate options only

option_1_ready.label: UNCONDITIONAL READY
option_1_ready.summary: Proceed without additional conditions or caveats
option_1_ready.description: Research demonstrates sufficient evidence for Ottoman naming shift (13th-17th centuries). 12/15 claims confirmed or strongly supported. Ottoman primary sources comprehensive. Administrative transition pattern well-documented. Ready for Phase E application and project implementation.
factual_basis: NM-001 (Double-naming 13-14c): ESTABLISHED via Ottoman genealogies + Byzantine sources
NM-003 (Single naming 17c): ESTABLISHED via 17th century defterleri + elite records
NM-005 (Arabic-Turkish semantic structure): ESTABLISHED via linguistic analysis + historical texts
NM-002 (15-16c transition in defterleri): STRONGLY_SUPPORTED via administrative records analysis
NM-012 (Cultural integration marker): STRONGLY_SUPPORTED via historical demography methodology
NM-014 (Non-Muslim naming independence): ESTABLISHED via Ottoman records comparison

requirements_satisfied.evidence: 14 primary sources including Ottoman archives, chronicles, genealogies, court records
Ottoman Studies scholarly consensus on naming shift established and documented
D2 evidence graph shows connected claim-evidence relationships; 39 sources support 15 claims
D3 causality chain maps 13th-17th century transition with documented endpoints

requirements_not_met.implication: Multiple plausible mechanisms; no single 'smoking gun' policy evidence
Peripheral Ottoman domains naming practices unstudied
Karakhanid and early Turkic naming origins incompletely documented

risk_factors: Mechanism uncertainty (MEDIUM-level risk): No explicit state naming policy found; causation inferred from context
Pre-Ottoman origins unclear (LOW-level risk): Does not affect documented Ottoman period claims
Regional knowledge gaps (LOW-level risk): Core Ottoman provinces well-documented; periphery less so but not contradicting

defensibility.basis: Core historical facts (double-naming existence, shift to single naming, timeline) well-established in multiple independent sources

recommended_for: Project implementation if mechanism details not essential
Content/video production where Ottoman naming shift narrative is sufficient
Public-facing materials where accessible narratives prioritized over mechanism precision
not_recommended_for: Academic publication requiring causal mechanism proof
Claims about universal Ottoman naming practices without regional qualification
caveats: Turkish state ideology as naming driver: INFERRED, not proven from explicit policy documents
Karakhanid comparison: LIMITED DATA makes pre-Ottoman narrative uncertain
Geographic uniformity: ASSUMED without peripheral region verification

option_2_conditional.label: CONDITIONAL READY (RECOMMENDED)
option_2_conditional.summary: Proceed with explicit conditions and caveats built into project outputs
option_2_conditional.description: Ottoman naming shift well-documented and defensible when explicitly qualified. Research quality sufficient for Phase E when accompanied by historiographic disclaimers acknowledging mechanism gaps and pre-Ottoman limitations. This option balances strong evidence base with transparent uncertainty handling.
factual_basis: Identical to Option 1: Core claims well-supported
PLUS explicit caveat layer protecting against over-interpretation

conditions.title: Pre-Islamic Naming Uncertainty Disclaimer
conditions.text: Project outputs must include: 'Ottoman naming practices draw from both Islamic and Turkic traditions. Pre-Islamic Turkic naming origins are reconstructed from linguistic analysis and limited historical sources; genealogical continuity from pre-Islamic to Ottoman periods is inferred rather than comprehensively documented.'
conditions.implementation_example: Add to project script/narration: 'While Seljuk and later Ottoman dynasties adopted Islamic names, earlier Turkic peoples' naming systems remain partially understood. The transition reflects broader Islamic cultural adoption in medieval Anatolia.'
conditions.necessity: CRITICAL — Without this disclaimer, pre-Islamic naming claims appear more certain than data supports

conditions.title: Causal Mechanism Uncertainty Acknowledged
conditions.text: Project must state: 'The Ottoman naming shift resulted from multiple interacting factors: state administrative centralization, Islamic cultural adoption, and institutional reinforcement. No single cause has been definitively proven; scholars debate whether political or religious factors were primary.'
conditions.implementation_example: Narration variant: 'Ottoman officials adopted Islamic naming practices during periods of state reform. Whether this reflected state policy, Islamic cultural appeal, or both remains historically debated.'
conditions.necessity: IMPORTANT — Prevents false certainty about state policy causation

conditions.title: Geographic Limitation Caveat
conditions.text: Project documentation must note: 'Ottoman core provinces (Anatolia, Istanbul region) naming patterns are well-documented. Naming practices in peripheral Ottoman territories (Balkans, Caucasus, Syria, Egypt) are less thoroughly studied and may have varied from core patterns.'
conditions.implementation_example: Footnote/caption: 'Ottoman defter analysis focuses on core provinces. Regional variation in peripheral domains remains under-researched.'
conditions.necessity: MODERATE — Prevents false universalism but not critical if project scope limited to core Ottoman regions

conditions.title: Administrative vs. Actual Practice Distinction
conditions.text: When citing defter evidence, distinguish: 'Ottoman administrative records show a naming shift (ESTABLISHED). Whether this reflects actual population naming practices or administrative recording standardization (or both) remains partially ambiguous (PROBABLE).'
conditions.implementation_example: Narration: 'Ottoman records from the 16th century show predominantly Islamic names. Whether this reflects genuine naming practice changes or how scribes recorded names is historically debated.'
conditions.necessity: MODERATE — Academic precision; less critical for general audiences

conditions.title: Contested Karakhanid Claim Handling
conditions.text: If project invokes NM-008 (Karakhanid single naming): 'Early Turkic dynasties like the Karakhanids (10th-11th centuries) are documented using single Islamic names. However, surviving Karakhanid sources are limited; double-naming among non-elite populations may have existed but gone undocumented.'
conditions.implementation_example: Optional omission if project timeline focuses on Ottoman period only; if including pre-Ottoman, add explicit uncertainty flag
conditions.necessity: LOW — Only applies if project extends to pre-Ottoman period

option_2_conditional.conditional_readiness_logic: Strong evidence + explicit conditions = HIGH CONFIDENCE DEFENSIBILITY. Conditions do not weaken factual claims; they accurately represent the state of historical knowledge.
requirements_satisfied: PLUS: Causal mechanism limitations explicitly stated
risk_factors: Academic critique risk: REDUCED via explicit caveats
Mechanism uncertainty: TRANSPARENT rather than hidden

defensibility.basis: Core facts well-established + uncertainty explicitly acknowledged = strongest possible defensible position

recommended_for: Video content aiming for both accuracy and accessibility
Projects where naming-shift narrative is central and mechanism details matter
Outputs subject to scholarly review or public challenge
benefits_over_option_1: Scholarly defensibility increased through transparent caveat-handling
Avoids false certainty that invites criticism
Allows full fact-base to shine without caveats undermining core narrative
Demonstrates research rigor and historiographic awareness
option_2_conditional.implementation_burden: MODERATE — Requires adding 3-5 caveats to project outputs; adds minimal length but ensures accuracy

option_3_blocked.label: BLOCKED (NOT APPLICABLE)
option_3_blocked.summary: No blocking conditions present. Research quality gates passed.
option_3_blocked.description: Phase D research does not contain E-LEG violations, fabrication, circular logic, or fundamental contradictions that would prevent synthesis and application. All major concerns are epistemological (mechanism uncertainty, source limitations) rather than integrity failures.

blocking_conditions_checked.evidence: No legal/rights issues, no plagiarism, no fabricated sources
Evidence chains coherent; no contradictory claims; Phase C red-team accepted all claims as at least probable
Source quality assessed in D5; known limitations documented but do not invalidate core claims
Historical sources; no living individual privacy concerns; no copyright conflicts beyond standard Ottoman Studies scholarship

option_3_blocked.conclusion: Research does not meet any blocking criteria. Proceed to Option 1 or Option 2; choice depends on project risk tolerance and scope.

summary_recommendation.rationale: Completeness score 0.80 indicates good but not perfect coverage. Contested claim (NM-008) and mechanism uncertainties (NM-004, NM-006, NM-009, NM-011, NM-013) suggest conditional approach is more defensible than unconditional. Core Ottoman naming shift is solid; peripheral uncertainties well-managed by explicit conditions.
summary_recommendation.secondary_recommendation: Option 1 (READY) acceptable for non-academic audiences; Option 2 necessary for scholarly credibility
summary_recommendation.rejected_recommendation: Option 3 (BLOCKED) is not applicable; no blocking conditions present

decision_options.action: Proceed with Phase E application. No additional conditions required.
decision_options.responsibility: Gatekeeper accepts research quality as-is; assumes project does not require mechanism-level precision

decision_options.action: Proceed with Phase E application. Integrate 5 conditions into project outputs via captions, footnotes, narration variants, or disclaimers.
decision_options.responsibility: Gatekeeper confirms conditions will be implemented; ensures project outputs include explicit caveats

decision_options.action: Return to Phase D for additional research on contested claims or mechanism clarification
decision_options.responsibility: Specify which claims require stronger evidence (e.g., 'Strengthen NM-008 Karakhanid evidence'; 'Clarify NM-004 diffusion mechanism')

decision_template_for_gatekeeper.gatekeeper_note: Decision authority: This agent does not decide; gatekeeper chooses based on project requirements, audience, and risk tolerance. Recommend Option B (CONDITIONAL) for balanced approach.
